target_customer: Gamers and digital content buyers; developers and publishers selling bundles
problem: Indie developers lacked a high-visibility way to sell games, and buyers wanted to choose their price and support charity.
business_model: Pay what you want bundles with revenue split between developers, charity and Humble; later storefront and Humble Monthly subscription

founders.name: Jeffrey Rosen
founders.background_notes: Wikipedia says Rosen of Wolfire Games conceived the bundle idea; YC page says he now angel invests in YC companies.

founders.name: John Graham
founders.background_notes: No bio on the YC page; Wikipedia says he and Rosen stepped down as CEO and COO in March 2019.

competitors.name: Steam bundle and holiday sales
competitors.what: Discounted game bundles on the dominant PC store, cited as inspiration

technical_complexity.rationale: A payment page, key delivery and DRM-free downloads; the hard part was operational scale at spikes, not research.

defensibility.rationale: Imitators appeared quickly (Indie Royale, IndieGala), but Humble held developer relationships and brand recognition.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Steam did not copy pay what you want; IGN bought Humble in October 2017.

market_need_then: Indie game boom in 2010 and demand for pay what you want pricing, charity tie-ins and DRM-free games, evidenced by the first bundle covered by TechCrunch on May 4, 2010.

branding.name_origin: The mission statement on the YC page ties Humble to charity and Bundle to the content packages; no founder statement on origin found.
branding.domain_note: humble.com is now the company domain; earlier humblebundle.com; purchase history not found.
branding.brand_signature: Pay what you want sliders and the charity split

rebrands.why: Separate the publishing label from the storefront brand

branding.community_and_virality: Bundles drew wide press coverage and repeated imitation by Indie Royale and IndieGala.

brand_strength.rationale: Imitated by competitors and widely covered, with over 500,000 Humble Monthly subscribers per the company; no formal brand study found.

pivots.to: Online storefront, Humble Monthly subscription and publishing
pivots.why: Branched out per the company description; exact dates not sourced

outcome_analysis: Humble Bundle used pay what you want pricing and a charity split to turn indie game sales into a recurring event, drew a 4.7 million dollar Sequoia round in April 2011, and widened into a storefront and monthly subscription. Imitators arrived but the brand held, and IGN Entertainment acquired it in October 2017 at an undisclosed price. The YC listing says it raised over 250 million dollars for charity.
notes: humble.com fetch was blocked by the tool, so no site content was read. Vator reported a 4.5 million round from the same filing; Fortune and Wikipedia say 4.7 million; the stage is not stated so it is other. YC page lists batch Winter 2011 though the company was founded in 2010. The 2017 date is October 13 per Wikipedia or October 16 per PocketGamer, so month only.
